To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a monoclonal antibody, 806, recognizing amplified/overexpressing wild-type epidermal growth-factor receptor in cancer but not in normal tissue was identified.
mAb 806 selectively reacts with tumors expressing high levels of EGFR and is not reactive with normal tissues, and that ΔEGFR, as opposed to other reports, is not found outside the brain.

a monoclonal antibody (806) that recognizes human cancers with EGFR ampliﬁcation/overexpression but does not react with normal tissues or cancers with normal EGFR level was developed and that the ΔEGFR mutation, previously reported in a variety of cancers, was found only in glioblastoma in a large tumor panel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a mAb that may prove useful for cancer diagnosis and therapy.
the generation of mAb reactivity profiles that can be used in clinical trials of mAb-based therapy of cancer.
the development of a novel mAb, 806, with a unique pattern of reactivity for tumors with EGFR overexpression/amplification, and the characterization of ΔEGFR as a glioblastoma-specific mutation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mAbs 806 and DH8. 3 are specific for tumors with amplified/overexpression of EGFR and ΔEGFR, respectively.
the mAb 806 recognizes a conformational epitope on the external domain of the EGFR that is present on ΔEGFR but absent from wtEGFR.

806 reacts with tumors that have amplification or overexpression of EGFR, whereas 528 reacts with all tumors that have amplifications and/or overexpression of wtEGFR and with normal tissues that have high EGFR levels, whereas DH8.3 reacts with ΔEGFR in glioblastoma only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mAb 806 recognizes tumors with EGFP amplification/over expression and is a potential candidate for cancer therapy.
806 is a novel anti-EGFR mAb that recognizes amplified/overexpressing wtEGFR, including ΔEGFR, and is useful in the detection of glioblastoma as well as lung and head and neck cancer.
mAb 806 recognizes amplified/overexpressing wtEGFR in glioblastoma as well as in a subset of epithelial cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
806 may be used as a companion diagnostic in the development of EGFR-targeted cancer therapies, e.g., in combination with erlotinib.
806 may be a useful reagent for the detection of EGFR amplification and for the selection of tumors with EGFR as a potential target for therapy.
806 is a promising reagent for the development of targeted cancer therapeutics.
